scenes.heading: SLIs, SLOs & SLAs
scenes.narration: These three acronyms turn vague promises about data quality into concrete, measurable commitments.

scenes.heading: The three terms
bullets: SLI: a Service Level Indicator — the actual metric you measure
SLO: a Service Level Objective — the internal target for that metric
SLA: a Service Level Agreement — the external contract with consequences
scenes.narration: An SLI is the raw measurement, such as the percentage of tables refreshed on time. An SLO is the target you set internally for that indicator, like ninety-nine percent. An SLA is a formal contract with a customer that carries penalties when the objective is missed, so it usually sits looser than the SLO.

scenes.heading: From measurement to commitment
scenes.narration: You start by picking an indicator that reflects what users actually feel, then set an achievable objective for it. Only some objectives graduate into a signed agreement with external consequences. Compliance is always evaluated over a rolling window rather than a single moment.

scenes.heading: SLO vs SLA in practice

right.title: SLA (external)
points: Set below the SLO on purpose

scenes.narration: The internal objective is deliberately more ambitious than any external agreement, giving you a safety margin. The agreement is what the customer sees and carries real financial consequences. Keeping the objective tighter means you catch trouble before you ever breach the contract.

scenes.heading: Checking an SLO in SQL
scenes.code:
-- SLI: % of runs completing within the freshness window
WITH runs AS (
  SELECT
    run_date,
    completed_at,
    expected_by
  FROM pipeline_runs
  WHERE run_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days'
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE completed_at <= expected_by)::float
    / COUNT(*) AS on_time_ratio,
  0.99 AS slo_target
FROM runs;
scenes.narration: This query computes the indicator over a thirty-day window: the fraction of runs that finished before their expected time. Comparing that ratio against the objective of ninety-nine percent tells you instantly whether you are meeting the target. Evaluating over a window smooths out a single unlucky day.

scenes.text: Measure what users feel (SLI), commit to a target you can hit (SLO), and keep any signed agreement (SLA) safely looser.
scenes.narration: Measure what users actually feel, set a target you can realistically hit, and always keep the external agreement looser than the internal objective.
